commands.name: BlendEdge
commands.description: Replaces selected solid edges with a Hermite blend surface that is trimmed and joined in.
commands.note: Hermite blend surface trimmed and stitched into the polysurface when both adjacent faces are planar; otherwise added between the two faces as a separate, untouched surface (not stitched in). Continuity=Tangency is a degree-3x3 G1 blend. Continuity=Curvature is a degree-5x3 blend whose cross-boundary second derivative is set to each face's own exact analytic directional second derivative (Ev2Der, not a finite difference), so its curvature vector matches each face's curvature exactly in that direction (numerically verified in tests/test_g2_blend.cpp for both flat and curved faces) - real G2 in the cross-boundary direction, not full surface-wide G2 in every direction, and it silently falls back to the plain G1 tangent at any sample where a face's own parametrization is singular there.

commands.name: BlendSrf
commands.description: Builds a Hermite blend surface between two picked surface edges, with a continuity option.
commands.note: Hermite blend between two picked surface edges. Continuity=Tangency is a degree-3x3 G1 blend. Continuity=Curvature is a degree-5x3 blend matching each surface's own exact directional second derivative at the boundary (Ev2Der), so its curvature vector matches exactly in the cross-boundary direction (see BlendEdge's own help and tests/test_g2_blend.cpp) - not a claim of full surface-wide G2.

commands.note: Toggles the decimal separator of printed numbers (Separator=Comma/Point).

commands.name: Delete
commands.description: Deletes the selected objects.

commands.name: DeleteFaces
commands.description: Removes picked faces from a polysurface or mesh.
commands.toolbars: Mesh Tools, Solid Tools, SubD Tools
commands.menu: Mesh / SubD | Edit Tools > Delete Faces | Solid | Solid Edit Tools > Delete Faces

commands.name: DeleteMeshNgons
commands.description: Deletes the n-gon faces from selected meshes.

commands.name: DeleteSubCrv
commands.description: Removes a picked portion of a curve, leaving the remaining pieces.
commands.menu: Curve | Curve Edit Tools > | Delete Subcurve

commands.name: Detail
commands.description: Adds a detail view to the active layout from two corner points.

commands.name: DevLoft
commands.description: Builds a ruled surface between two rail curves with rulings chosen to minimize twist, approximately developable.
commands.note: Ruled surface whose rulings are chosen to minimise the twist between the rails; approximately developable.

commands.name: Diameter
commands.description: Reports the diameter of a picked circle or arc, optionally marking it with a dimension.

commands.name: DigBeep
commands.description: Toggles a terminal bell for each point digitized with the Dig commands.
commands.note: Stored flag: when on, Digitize/DigCamera/DigClick/DigLine/DigSection/DigSketch print a terminal bell (\\a) for each digitized point - a real, if minimal, stand-in for the audible beep real digitizer hardware would make. Fires under any of the three DigConnect protocols, including Simulated (DigConnect Protocol=Simulated needs no hardware at all).

commands.name: DigCalibrate
commands.description: Calibrates the digitizer from three points: origin, a point on the X axis and a point on the Y axis.
commands.note: 3-point calibration (origin, +X point, +Y point) into the active CPlane.

commands.name: DigCamera
commands.description: Digitizes an eye point and a target point and aims the active viewport's camera from one to the other.
commands.note: Digitizes two points - eye, then target - and points the active viewport's camera from the first at the second, both run through the digitizer's calibration/unit scale exactly like every other Dig* command. DigConnect first (Protocol=Simulated needs no hardware: DigConnect Protocol=Simulated, then click twice in the viewport).

commands.name: DigClick
commands.description: Digitizes one point and prints it without adding an object.
commands.note: Digitizes one point and prints it, the same as Digitize but without adding an object. Note that unlike a real digitizer's hardware button, DigClick here is just another typed command name: this engine feeds any typed line to whatever command is already running, so DigClick can only ever fire when *no* other command is waiting for a point - it cannot interrupt one the way a real digitizer's stylus click would. It still forwards the point it reads via CommandEngine::FeedPoint, a no-op today for the same reason (nothing is ever waiting for a point at that moment either), kept for a future point-prompting command that might check right after it runs.

commands.name: DigDisconnect
commands.description: Disconnects the digitizer.

commands.name: Digitize
commands.description: Reads one point from the connected digitizer and adds it as a point object.
commands.note: Reads one point from the connected digitizer's calibrated stream and adds it as a point object. DigConnect first: Protocol=Ascii for real hardware, File to replay a fixture of recorded points, or Simulated to feed points from mouse clicks (or, in a --script test, a plain "x,y,z" token) with no hardware at all - all three protocols run the identical read/calibrate/add-object logic here.

commands.name: DigLine
commands.description: Digitizes two points and joins them into a line.
commands.note: Digitizes two points and joins them into a line (a 2-point polyline curve). DigConnect first; Protocol=Simulated needs no hardware, just two clicks in the viewport (or two "x,y,z" tokens in a --script test).

commands.name: DigPause
commands.description: Pauses input from the digitizer.

commands.name: DigScale
commands.description: Sets the scale applied to raw digitizer readings before calibration.
commands.note: Sets the device-to-model unit scale applied to raw digitizer readings, before calibration.

commands.name: DigSection
commands.description: Digitizes a sequence of points and joins them into a polyline curve.
commands.note: Digitizes a sequence of points (Protocol=File/Ascii: every point currently queued, up to 5000; Protocol=Simulated: click points in the viewport, Enter when done) and joins them into a polyline curve, standing in for tracing a physical cross-section with a digitizer arm.

commands.name: DigSketch
commands.description: Digitizes a sequence of points into a polyline curve; behaves the same as DigSection.
commands.note: Identical to DigSection - digitizes a sequence of points into a polyline curve - named separately because Rhino offers both for the same real-world action of tracing a shape freehand with the stylus.

commands.name: Dim
commands.description: Adds a linear dimension between two picked points.

commands.name: DimAligned
commands.description: Adds a dimension measured along the line between two picked points.

commands.name: DimAngle
commands.description: Adds an angle dimension from a vertex and two direction points.

commands.name: DimArea

commands.name: DimCreaseAngle
commands.description: Dimensions the angle between two lines or between the first planar faces of two objects.
commands.note: Angle between two lines or the first planar faces of two objects; no face-level sub-object picking on polysurfaces (nothing in this app has that yet), so a polysurface always measures from its first planar face.

commands.name: DimCurveLength
commands.description: Adds a dimension giving a selected curve's length.

commands.name: DimDiameter
commands.description: Adds a diameter dimension to a selected circle or arc.

commands.name: DimOrdinate
commands.description: Adds ordinate dimensions showing each picked feature point's offset from a base point.

commands.name: DimRadius
commands.description: Adds a radius dimension to a selected circle or arc.

commands.name: DimRecenterText
commands.description: Rebuilds dimension text at its original default position.
commands.note: Rebuilds the text at the position it was created with.

commands.name: DimRotated
commands.description: Adds a linear dimension measured along a chosen angle.

commands.name: DimVolume
commands.description: Adds a dimension showing the volume of a selected solid.

commands.name: Dir
commands.description: Shows each curve's direction or surface's normal with arrows, and lets you flip or swap them.
commands.note: Reports each curve's start point/tangent or surface's centre point/normal in the command history AND draws a real, clickable direction-arrow glyph at that exact location in every open viewport (ui/DirectionArrows.cpp, ComputeDirArrow()/FlipObject() in doc/SceneObject.h/.cpp) - clicking it calls the same FlipObject() reversal Flip itself uses, not a second implementation. The glyph-click path is mouse-only and, like every other mouse-driven interaction in this app (Gumball, MappingGizmo, ...), is not exercised by the headless tests/smoke.sh harness; the glyph's own computed geometry is independently verifiable headlessly because ComputeDirArrow() is the exact function both Dir's printed origin/direction and the glyph's drawn position/direction come from - a script confirms the printed numbers, then re-runs Dir after a plain Flip and confirms they invert.

commands.name: DirectionalLight
commands.description: Adds a directional light defined by a start point and a direction.

commands.name: DisableClippingPlane
commands.description: Turns off the enabled clipping planes so they stop cutting the view.

commands.name: DisableOsnap
commands.description: Toggles all object snaps off or back on.

commands.name: DisplayCommandPrompt
commands.description: Shows the command-line window.
commands.note: Shows the command-line window (see CommandPrompt).

commands.name: DisplayProperties
commands.description: Opens the display-properties panel.

commands.name: Distance
commands.description: Reports the distance between two picked points.

commands.name: Distribute
commands.description: Spaces selected objects evenly along the X, Y or Z direction.

commands.name: Divide

commands.description: Splits selected SubDs into separate pieces along their crease edges.
commands.menu: Surface | Surface Edit Tools > | Divide Surface on Creases

commands.name: DocumentProperties
commands.description: Opens the document-properties panel.

commands.name: DocumentPropertiesPage
commands.description: Opens the document-properties panel.

commands.name: DollyZoom
commands.description: Sets a new lens length and moves the camera so the target keeps its on-screen size.
commands.toolbars: Lens Length, Render Sidebar, Set View, View
commands.note: Type the new lens length; recomputes the camera distance so the target keeps its on-screen size (the 'Vertigo' effect).

commands.name: Domain
commands.description: Shows or sets the parameter domain of selected curves or surfaces.

commands.name: Dot
commands.description: Creates a text dot: a point object that carries a short text label.

commands.name: DownloadLibraryTextures
commands.description: Explains that Dino 8 has no online texture library and makes no network calls, so nothing is downloaded.

commands.name: DraftAnglePoint
commands.description: Reports the draft angle at a picked surface point relative to the pull direction.
commands.note: Draft angle at the picked surface point relative to the DraftAngleAnalysis pull direction (world Z by default).

commands.name: DragCopy
commands.description: Toggles leaving a copy behind when a gumball translate drag moves the original.
commands.note: When on, a gumball translate drag leaves a copy at the start position and moves the original; Alt inverts this for one drag.

commands.name: DragMode
commands.description: Chooses the plane in which the gumball's free handle drags: CPlane, World, UVN, View or ControlPolygon.
commands.note: Sets the plane the gumball's centre (Free) handle drags in: CPlane and World are exact; UVN and ControlPolygon (which need a surface/mesh control point, not a whole-object gumball) fall back to the view-perpendicular plane, same as View.

commands.description: Scales gumball translate drags by a percentage, so 50 moves the selection half as far as the mouse.

commands.name: DupAnnotationStyle
commands.description: Duplicates an annotation style under a new name given by the NewName option.

commands.name: DupBorder

commands.menu: Curve | Curve From Objects > | Duplicate Edge

commands.name: DupFaceBorder

commands.menu: Curve | Curve From Objects > | Duplicate Face Border

commands.name: DupLayer
commands.description: Copies the current or a named layer under a new name, optionally with its objects.
commands.note: Copies the current layer (or Layer=name) under a new name (Name=); Objects=No skips copying its objects.

commands.name: DupMeshEdge
commands.description: Copies picked naked mesh edges as curves or lines.
commands.menu: Curve | Curve From Objects > | Duplicate Mesh Edge

commands.menu: Mesh | Edit Tools > | Extract > | Hole Boundary

commands.description: Stores a model point with its latitude, longitude and elevation in document user text.

commands.name: Echo
commands.description: Turns echoing of command text to the command history on.

commands.name: EdgeContinuity
commands.description: Measures gap, tangent angle and curvature difference between two curves or surface edges and draws markers.
commands.note: Samples one edge against the closest points of the other: gap, tangent angle, curvature difference; hairs drawn as an overlay.

commands.name: EdgeSrf
commands.description: Makes a surface bounded by two to four edge curves; shares the NetworkSrf implementation.

commands.name: EditClippingDrawings
commands.description: Selects the clipping-drawing curves so ordinary curve-editing commands can modify them.

commands.name: EditLightByHighlight

commands.name: EditLightByLooking
commands.description: Aims the view through a light; Enter saves the view's eye and target back into the light.
commands.note: Aims the view through the light; Enter saves the view's new eye/target back into the light's position/direction.

commands.name: EditPythonScript
commands.description: Opens a Python file in the Script Editor panel, which runs it with the embedded interpreter.
commands.note: Opens the given .py file in the Script Editor panel; the panel's Run button detects the .py extension and dispatches to the embedded Python 3 interpreter (same engine as RunPythonScript), while .lua files there still run as Lua.

commands.name: EditScript
commands.description: Opens the Lua Script Editor.
commands.note: Opens the Lua Script Editor.

commands.name: Ellipse
commands.description: Draws an ellipse from its center and the end points of its two axes.

commands.name: Ellipsoid

commands.note: Solid/Gradient/Sky/Image backgrounds; Image is drawn as a real lat-long (equirectangular) environment around the camera's own view direction (GlRenderer::DrawEnvironmentBackground) in the interactive Rendered display mode, and the same way (direction-mapped, so it surrounds the camera rather than stretching to the frame) by a raytraced Render/RenderPreview/RenderArctic/RenderBlowup (PathTracer::SkyColor) - the live RayTracedViewport GPU preview still falls back to a solid colour for Image (GpuRaytracer has no env-map sampling).

commands.description: Reports the coordinates of a picked point, with options to label it with a dot or leader.

commands.name: ExplodeBlock
commands.description: Replaces selected block instances with copies of the objects in their definition.

commands.description: Writes the selected objects to a file in a chosen format.

commands.name: ExportBitmaps
commands.description: Copies every texture used by materials into a chosen folder.
commands.note: Copies every referenced material texture into a folder (textures are never embedded).

commands.name: ExportClippingDrawings
commands.description: Exports the clipping-plane section drawings to a file.

commands.name: ExportClippingSectionInfo
commands.description: Writes the clipping-section data to a text file.

commands.name: ExportLinkedBlocks
commands.description: Saves a block definition's objects to a .3dm file; the block remains embedded.

commands.name: ExportRuiFile
commands.description: Writes the toolbar tabs and buttons to a small XML toolbar file.
commands.note: Writes the toolbar tabs and buttons as a small .rui-style XML file.

commands.name: ExportWithOrigin
commands.description: Exports a copy of the selection translated so a picked point lands at the origin.
commands.note: Translates copies of the selection so the picked point lands at 0,0,0 before writing them; SVG/PDF (page-space view drawings, not object-space geometry) export the plain view instead.

commands.name: Extend
commands.description: Extends the end of each curve nearer a picked point until its tangent reaches that point.
commands.note: Extends the end of each curve nearer the picked point until its tangent line reaches that point (Enter extends both ends by a fixed 10% of the domain instead).

commands.name: ExtendCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Extends a curve that lies on a surface, along that surface, by a given length.
commands.menu: Curve | Extend Curve > | Curve on Surface

commands.name: ExtendDynamic
commands.description: Extends a curve end by a typed length.

commands.name: ExtendSrf
commands.description: Extends a surface edge by a given distance, with options for smooth or line extension.

commands.name: ExtractAnalysisMesh
commands.description: Converts the displayed analysis mesh of selected objects into mesh objects by running Mesh.

commands.name: ExtractBadSrf

commands.name: ExtractControlPolygon
commands.description: Creates a polyline through the control points of selected curves.

commands.name: ExtractCurvatureGraph
commands.description: Creates the curvature comb of selected curves as curve objects.
commands.note: The curvature comb as curve objects (Scale= Density=).

commands.name: ExtractCustomMappingObject
commands.description: Creates a rectangle curve from the custom mapping frame stored on an object.
commands.note: Extracts the real custom-mapping frame ApplyCustomMapping stores on the object (origin, x/y axes, size) as a rectangle curve; other mapping types (Planar/Box/...) are bounding-box projections with no separate mapping object to extract.

commands.name: ExtractIsocurve
commands.description: Extracts isoparametric curves from a surface at picked locations in the U or V direction.
commands.menu: Curve | Curve From Objects > | Extract Isocurve

commands.name: ExtractLineTypeSegments

commands.name: ExtractMeshEdges

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByAspectRatio
commands.description: Extracts the mesh faces whose longest-to-shortest edge ratio lies between a minimum and maximum.
commands.note: Registered through a table-driven command family rather than a standalone Reg(...) call; see the source file for the shared implementation.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByDraftAngle
commands.description: Extracts the mesh faces whose angle from the construction-plane normal lies between a minimum and maximum.
commands.note: Registered through a table-driven command family rather than a standalone Reg(...) call; see the source file for the shared implementation.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByEdgeLength
commands.description: Extracts the mesh faces whose longest edge length lies between a minimum and maximum.
commands.note: Registered through a table-driven command family rather than a standalone Reg(...) call; see the source file for the shared implementation.

commands.name: ExtractMeshPart
commands.description: Extracts the connected part of a mesh under a picked point into a new mesh.

commands.name: ExtractNonManifoldMeshEdges
commands.description: Creates curves along the non-manifold edges of selected meshes.

commands.description: Restores the pre-cage originals of captive objects as new copies.

Unlike the session-only HoleFeature/PipeFeature/SquishFeature/SubDPackFeature side tables (Document.h), CageBinding's captive originals are written to and read back from the .3dm (io/File3dm.cpp: each original travels as a hidden geometry component tagged Dino8.CaptiveOriginalOf/Dino8.CaptiveCageOf/Dino8.CaptiveLocal, plus a small Dino8.CageBindingsMeta JSON sidecar for the cage's own nx/ny/nz/lattice), so the original is still there to extract after the file is closed and reopened.

commands.description: Recovers the original rail curve from a pipe surface or mesh made with Pipe.

commands.name: ExtractRenderMesh
commands.description: Creates mesh objects from the render meshes of selected surfaces, polysurfaces or SubDs.

commands.description: Pulls picked faces out of a polysurface as separate surfaces, optionally leaving the original.
commands.toolbars: Solid Tools, Curve Drawing, Geometry Fix, Main, Main2, Popup, Solids Sidebar, SubD Sidebar, Surface Sidebar

commands.name: ExtractSubCrv
commands.description: Copies picked portions of curves out as new curves, optionally joining them.
commands.menu: Curve | Curve From Objects > | Extract Curve

commands.name: ExtractUVMesh
commands.description: Creates a flat mesh in a surface's U-V space, or at a mesh's texture coordinates.
commands.note: A flat mesh in the surface's UV space (scaled to its approximate size) or at a mesh's texture coordinates.

commands.name: ExtractWireframe
commands.description: Creates isocurves and edge curves from selected surfaces or polysurfaces.
commands.menu: Curve | Curve From Objects > | Extract Wireframe

commands.name: ExtrudeCrv
commands.description: Extrudes selected curves along the construction-plane normal by a typed or picked distance.
commands.toolbars: Extrude, Extrude Solid, Solids Sidebar, Surface Creation, Surface Sidebar
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Planar Curve > | Straight | Surface | Extrude Curve > | Straight | SubD | Extrude Curve > | Straight

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvAlongCrv
commands.description: Sweeps a profile curve along a path by pure translation, without rotating the profile.
commands.toolbars: Extrude, Extrude Solid, Surface Creation, Surface Sidebar
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Planar Curve > | Along Curve | Surface | Extrude Curve > | Along Curve | SubD | Extrude Curve > | Along Curve
commands.note: Exact translational sweep (sum surface); the profile is not rotated along the path.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvTapered
commands.description: Extrudes a curve to a scaled copy of itself, set by a draft angle, as a ruled surface.
commands.toolbars: Extrude, Extrude Solid, Surface Creation, Surface Sidebar
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Planar Curve > | Tapered | Surface | Extrude Curve > | Tapered
commands.note: Ruled surface to a copy of the profile scaled about its centroid by the draft angle (exact for circles, approximate corners).

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvToPoint
commands.description: Extrudes selected curves to a single apex point, forming a cone-like surface.
commands.toolbars: Extrude, Extrude Solid, Surface Creation, Surface Sidebar
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Planar Curve > | To Point | Surface | Extrude Curve > | To Point | SubD | Extrude Curve > | To Point

commands.name: ExtrudeMesh
commands.description: Extrudes selected mesh faces or edge loops by a distance along a chosen direction.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrf
commands.description: Extrudes selected surfaces by a distance into solids.
commands.toolbars: Extrude Solid, Solid Creation, Solid Editing, Solids Sidebar, Solid Tools
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Surface> | Extrude Surface to Boundary> | Straight

commands.name: ExtrudeSrfAlongCrv
commands.description: Sweeps a surface's mesh along a path curve by translation to make a closed mesh solid.
commands.toolbars: Extrude Solid, Solid Editing, Solid Tools
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Surface> | Extrude Surface to Boundary> | Along Curve
commands.note: Closed mesh solid: the surface's render mesh swept along the path (translation only).

commands.name: ExtrudeSrfTapered
commands.description: Extrudes a surface's mesh along the construction-plane normal, scaled by a draft angle, into a closed mesh solid.
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Surface> | Extrude Surface to Boundary> | Tapered
commands.note: Closed mesh solid: the surface's render mesh extruded along the CPlane normal and scaled by DraftAngle=.

commands.description: Extrudes a surface's mesh to a picked apex, forming a closed mesh solid.
commands.menu: Solid | Extrude Surface> | Extrude Surface to Boundary> | To Point
commands.note: Closed mesh solid: the surface's render mesh coned to the picked apex.

commands.name: ExtrudeSubD
commands.description: Extrudes picked SubD faces, or the whole SubD, by a distance in a chosen direction.

commands.name: Fair
commands.description: Smooths selected curves by reducing their curvature variation, with options to preserve ends.

commands.name: FileExplorer
commands.description: Opens the working folder in the file explorer.
commands.note: Opens the OS file manager (Explorer/Finder/xdg-open) at the working folder, the current document's folder, or the current directory, in that order; only prints the folder in headless/script mode.

commands.name: Fill
commands.description: Fills picked SubD hole boundaries with faces, using single-face, fan or triangulated patterns.

commands.name: Fillet
commands.description: Rounds the corner between two curves with an arc of a given radius.
commands.note: Exact for lines; for other curves the local tangent lines at the picks are used (approximate).

commands.name: FilletCorners
commands.description: Rounds the corners of polylines with tangent arcs, skipping corners where the radius does not fit.
commands.note: Rounds polyline corners with a tangent arc; corners where the radius does not fit are skipped.

commands.name: FilletEdge
commands.description: Rounds selected solid edges with a rolling-ball fillet.

commands.name: FilletSrf
commands.description: Creates a rolling-ball fillet surface between two surfaces, trimming both when the inputs are planar.

commands.name: Loft
commands.description: Builds a surface that passes exactly through selected curves in order.
commands.note: Calls the kernel's exact interpolating Brep::Loft: every selected curve lies exactly on the result (measured and printed), Normal is cubic in the loft direction and Style=Straight is linear (sharp at every section). Curves are first made consistent - open curves reversed to run the same way, closed curves reversed to circulate the same way and re-seamed to the point nearest the previous curve's start; a mix of open and closed curves is refused with the reason. Closed planar curves are capped into a polysurface solid (Cap=Yes, the default; Cap=No leaves the periodic surface). Closed=Yes lofts on from the last curve back to the first (kernel Brep::Loft closed=true: a periodic interpolation through every curve, a closed surface with no ends and no caps; at least three curves, refused with the reason otherwise; recorded in History and editable with EditHistory closed=yes|no; with the default SeamAlign=Yes each closed curve is re-seamed to the start point that best matches the previous curve point for point (minimum twist), and a twist left between the last curve and the first is reported). Loose/Tight aren't distinguishable here and aren't offered. SeamAlign=No uses the sections exactly as given (a closed curve whose start point or direction differs from its neighbour's then twists the wall); the default Yes reverses/re-seams them first. StartTangent=<name> / EndTangent=<name> (curve objects named with SetObjectName; their control points are the wall's dS/dv vectors at the first / last curve, e.g. a copy of a circle section scaled by a and lifted by b is the field (a x, a y, b)) with StartWeight= / EndWeight= (default 1) call the kernel's Hermite-type Brep::LoftWithSectionTangents, exact for rational sections (the tangent curve needs the section's weights, or to be a constant field); two curves with both tangents give a cubic Hermite wall; the sections are used as given, the result is not recorded in History. Spacing=Chord|Uniform|Centripetal chooses the loft-direction station parameters (kernel Brep::LoftSpacing: averaged control-point chord lengths by default, equal parameter steps for Uniform, square-root chord lengths for Centripetal); every spacing interpolates every section exactly, only the shape between sections changes. If the kernel refuses a loft, the older control-point fit is used and the reason printed. Continuity=Position|Tangency|Curvature (G0/G1/G2, with AngleTol= in degrees and CurvTol= in 1/length; none given = everything above unchanged) asks for a click near an edge of an existing surface and calls the kernel's NurbsSurface::LoftMatched: the first or last section (whichever lies nearer that surface) is made identical to the edge and the next rows are rewritten by MatchEdge; the finished uncapped surface is MEASURED along the edge (position gap, tangent angle, cross-edge and Gaussian curvature difference) and every section's deviation from it is printed, and the request is refused with the kernel's reason (G0 not met, a closed section, a loft folding back over the adjacent surface, a degree too low, a measured angle / curvature above tolerance) building nothing. A continuity result is not recorded in History (the reason is printed).

commands.name: MatchSrf
commands.description: Moves a surface edge row to meet a target surface with position or tangent continuity.
commands.note: Moves the picked surface's boundary control row onto the target (Position); Tangency also aligns the next row's step to the target's tangent/normal. Against a target surface edge, Position/Tangency/Curvature all try the exact kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdge() construction first (real NURBS algebra, not moved-and-hoped-for control points) - Curvature additionally matches the cross-boundary second derivative, real G2, not just G1 (see kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdge()'s own doc comment). Against a target CURVE (rational arcs and circles included) the exact kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdgeToCurve() construction is tried first: the edge becomes the curve exactly and, for Tangency/Curvature, the surface keeps its own cross-boundary tangent (and curvature) along it. Follow=Yes (with Continuity=Tangency or Curvature and a target curve lying on a host surface; you then click the host surface as a third pick) makes the edited surface leave the curve in the HOST's tangent plane - its own cross direction rotated into that plane at its own speed - and, with Curvature, take the HOST's second fundamental form along the curve (G2 to the host) (kernel::NurbsSurface::MatchEdgeToCurveFollowing); rational surfaces work, and a curve that is not on the host is refused with nothing changed. Curvature has no approximate fallback when the exact match itself fails (an edge the exact algebra cannot match; periodic surfaces, curves and hosts are matched through their clamped equivalent and a target of too low a degree is elevated exactly first) - it fails closed with a diagnostic rather than silently downgrading to G1/G0.

commands.name: NetworkSrf
commands.description: Builds a surface from a network of curves.
commands.note: Two curves give an exact ruled surface. Three or four curves that close into a loop within the document tolerance call the kernel's exact Coons patch (CoonsPatchTriangular / CoonsPatch: all boundaries reproduced exactly, corners within tolerance closed first, any order or direction, measured boundary deviation printed); a set that does not close, or that the kernel refuses, prints why and falls back to the old bilinear Coons patch fitted as a degree-3 surface. Five or more curves that close into a loop within the document tolerance are chained (any order or direction), joined into one loop and trimmed out of the kernel's least-squares NurbsSurface::FitPatch surface as one B-rep face (approximate, not an interpolating Coons patch: the worst deviation from the curves and the trimmed edge's deviation are printed and a miss of the tolerance is flagged); a set that does not close, or whose loop folds over its best-fit plane, prints why and uses the first 4 curves as before. Four or more curves that CROSS in their interiors form a curve network: the kernel (NurbsSurface::FitCurveNetwork) sorts them into two directions by where they meet, requires every curve to meet every curve of the other direction within the document tolerance, fits one NURBS surface (cubic where the net allows) through the curves and the meetings, and prints the measured distance of EVERY input curve from it (approximate least-squares fit over the curves' bounding rectangle, untrimmed); a network that misses the tolerance, whose curves do not all meet, or whose order is not a regular grid prints why and the older behaviour runs. Continuity=Position|Tangency|Curvature (G0/G1/G2, with AngleTol= in degrees and CurvTol= in 1/length; none given = everything above unchanged) asks for a click near an edge of an existing surface and, for a curve network of four or more curves, calls the kernel's continuity-aware FitCurveNetwork: the input curve lying on that edge is fitted with the adjacent surface's tangent plane (and second fundamental form) as a heavily weighted constraint, the finished surface is MEASURED along the edge (position gap, tangent angle, cross-edge and Gaussian curvature difference) and printed, and the request is refused with the kernel's reason when G0 is not met, the adjacent plane is too steep, or the measured angle / curvature / curve deviation exceeds the tolerance. A 2-curve or loop selection has no continuity option (refused with that reason). A continuity result is not recorded in History (the reason is printed).

commands.name: Reflect
commands.description: Mirrors selected surfaces or meshes across a picked plane and welds the copy to the original into one symmetric object.
commands.note: A one-shot 'make symmetric' tool: mirrors the selection across the picked plane and welds the original and its mirror image into a single symmetric whole. A selection made entirely of SubDs (one or more) comes back as a real, editable SubD (kernel::SubD::Symmetrize, folded together via SubD::BooleanToSubD when there's more than one); any other input kind comes back as a single mesh (CreateSolid's MergeAndWeld). Rhino's live symmetric-SubD-editing mode - where every later edit to one half re-applies to the other - needs an ongoing mirror-constraint system this app doesn't have; this covers the one-shot case honestly instead of only printing guidance.

commands.name: Shell
commands.description: Hollows a closed solid to a wall thickness, optionally opening picked faces.
commands.note: Hollows a closed solid. With no face clicked to remove/open and no per-face thickness override, a polysurface whose faces are all planar and convex (a box or other simple polyhedron) now calls the kernel's exact ShellConvexPlanar first, giving a real B-rep result (exact volume, no tessellation) instead of a mesh; it fails open to the existing mesh construction (outer minus inward vertex-normal offset) for a curved or non-convex solid, or a thickness beyond that shape's own offset feasibility. Optionally click face(s) of a polysurface solid to remove/open before entering thickness (Enter with none picked keeps the old fully-closed behavior): the picked face(s) are dropped from the outer surface, the remainder gets the inward offset, and a rim mesh connects the two boundary loops - a real open shell (cup/case) for a single face, or a group of mutually-adjacent faces, on a simple box-like solid; a selection that would leave a non-manifold or multi-piece remainder is rejected with a warning rather than producing bad geometry, and mesh-only solids (no polysurface to pick faces on) still only support the fully-closed form. After face removal you can also click additional face(s) and type a thickness for each (repeat, then Enter for the default Thickness on the rest): every kept face's vertices then solve to the exact intersection of its own neighbours' offset planes, so two faces with different thickness meet in a real mitered corner rather than an average - numerically verified for a box (see tests/surface_script.txt) and, by the same plane-intersection algebra, correct for any solid whose kept faces are all planar (prisms and other polyhedra). If any kept face is curved, per-face overrides are detected and dropped for that solid (warned), falling back to the single default Thickness everywhere on it rather than applying an unverified per-triangle offset to a curved surface.

commands.name: SplitRefitSurface

commands.name: Sweep1
commands.description: Sweeps cross-section curves along one rail curve to build a surface.
commands.note: A single cross section calls the kernel's exact Brep::Sweep1 (rotation-minimizing-frame transport and skin; still an uncapped surface, periodic when the rail is closed, same as before) and records History (History On) for UpdateHistory to rebuild against the rail/section's current shape; two or more cross sections call the kernel's exact Brep::Sweep1Sections (each section anchored on the rail - a closed planar one where the rail crosses its plane - decoded in its rotation-minimizing frame, blended between neighbours and skinned through the stations: every section reproduced exactly, the wall measured against the exact blended sections between stations and held to the document tolerance, retried at up to 256 stations; an uncapped surface; closed cross sections must already share a seam and direction, the kernel refuses seams more than 60 degrees apart; with History On it records {rail, section 1, section 2, ...} and rebuilds when the rail or a section is edited, a rebuild the kernel refuses keeping the old wall with the reason printed); it falls back, with the reason printed, to the old sampled approximation (24 samples per section, fitted to a degree-3 surface) when the kernel refuses (closed rail, a section plane the rail never crosses or contains, two sections at one station, mismatched seams) or misses the document tolerance. Cap=Yes (default No) turns the sweep of a closed planar cross section into a closed B-rep solid with the kernel's own capping (two planar end caps; the section may sit anywhere along the rail and several cross sections are capped too; recorded for History); an open or non-planar section, or a fallback construction, keeps the uncapped surface and prints why. A closed rail that is an exact planar circle is built as the section revolved once about the rail's axis (Brep::Revolve: an exact rational surface, e.g. a true torus, measured against the revolved section and printed), and with Cap=Yes as a closed one-face solid; any other closed rail keeps the kernel's periodic skin.

commands.name: Sweep2
commands.description: Sweeps cross-section curves along two rail curves to build a surface.
commands.note: A single cross section calls the kernel's exact Brep::Sweep2 (two-rail frame transport and skin; still an uncapped surface, same as before) and records History (History On) for UpdateHistory to rebuild against the rails/section's current shape. Two or more cross sections call the kernel's Brep::Sweep2Sections (each section decoded in its own station's two-rail frame, blended between neighbours and skinned through the stations: every section reproduced, wall edges within the document tolerance of the rails when the sections touch them, measured and printed; closed cross sections must already share a seam and direction, the kernel does not align them; with History On it records {rail 1, rail 2, section 1, section 2, ...} and rebuilds when a rail or a section is edited, a rebuild the kernel refuses keeping the old wall with the reason printed); it falls back, with the reason printed, to the old approximated two-rail-scaled sweep fitted to a degree-3 surface when the kernel refuses (crossing section anchors, rails that touch at an interior station, a section where the rails touch) or misses the document tolerance; two closed rails give a cyclic sweep whose wall is closed round the ring (seam at the first section, sections ordered round both rails), and rails meeting at an end give a wall pinched to a point there. Cap=Yes (default No) caps a closed planar cross section's sweep into a closed B-rep solid (single section, or the multi-section wall) with the kernel's own capping; anything that cannot be capped keeps the surface and prints why.

commands.name: Symmetry
commands.description: Makes a mirrored copy that stays linked to its source and updates when the source changes.
commands.note: Builds a live mirrored copy: like Mirror Copy=Yes, but the copy carries a real link (Document::SymmetryLink, a side table keyed by the copy's id, same pattern as HoleFeature/PipeFeature/SquishFeature) back to the source object and the mirror plane it was built from. UpdateSymmetryPairs re-derives the copy's geometry from the source's *current* shape every frame (the same per-frame hook UpdateCageCaptives already uses to keep CageEdit's captives following a moved cage - Application::Frame, cmd_solidtools.cpp), so editing the source keeps the mirrored copy in sync automatically with no rebuild command needed - a genuine live constraint, not a one-time bake. RemoveSymmetry breaks the link.

commands.name: VariableBlendSrf
commands.description: Builds a blend surface between two surfaces whose tangency varies along the join.
commands.menu: Surface | Variable Fillet/Chamfer/Blend > | Variable Blend Surfaces
commands.note: A genuine independent blend-tangent variant of BlendSrf (not the rolling-ball fillet VariableFilletSrf uses): the same BuildBlendSurfaceG1/G2 Hermite/quintic blend between two picked surface edges, with the blend's own cross-section width interpolated linearly along the rail from Width= to EndWidth=, the same piecewise-linear-along-the-rail technique FilletTwoSurfacesCommand uses for Radius=/EndRadius=. Continuity=Curvature gets the same real, numerically-verified G2 cross-boundary curvature match as BlendSrf (see tests/test_g2_blend.cpp and tests/test_variable_blend.cpp), independent of the width, which no fixed-cross-section rolling-ball fillet construction can do except at one coincidental radius.

commands.name: VariableFilletSrf

commands.menu: Surface | Variable Fillet/Blend/Chamfer > | Variable Fillet Surfaces
commands.note: Radius interpolated linearly along the spine from Radius= to EndRadius= (spine itself uses the average radius, an approximation for strongly varying radii).

commands.name: VariableOffsetSrf
